agree.reason: The invoice offer, the dated meeting, the single concrete contract term and the 20-mile chain gap give a skeptical director a reason to check the claim rather than file it as the usual yearly complaint, though nothing makes the cost of inaction concrete enough to force her hand.

honest.reason: It rightly drops the 'third will close' claim and admits it can't link the nine closures to rates, but it stretches an average loss into 'every one of those… costs us money' and implies the whole 22 percent ('a fifth') is filled at a loss, when only the 20 generics are known to lose money.

works_the_facts.reason: The figures are restated but never worked: there is no rough dollar scale of the loss and no 'if nothing changes by July 1' arithmetic, so the $1.80 stays an abstract average.

right_comparison.reason: It describes the alternative accurately for the 14 counties (the nearest chain is more than 20 miles away) and adds the trend of nine closures in two years without overstating why they closed.

qualification.reason: The July 1 renewal and May 1 meeting give dates, but the key hedge, that two pharmacies will stop filling 'if nothing changes,' has no checkable date or threshold, and the brand-drug offset is left vague.

objections.reason: It meets 'they complain every year' with an offer to share invoices, 'members have chains' with the 20-mile fact, and 'the PBM sets rates' with the plan's control of the contract terms, and it raises no objection that the facts already settle.

fit.reason: It is a one-page open letter in a plain voice, addressed and signed correctly, and works for both the plan and the newspapers.
